chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: It's awkwardly worded, but it means 339 out of 1628 PB were delivered via unicast; the other 1628-339 were multicast.

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: What does that tell me? Is this good?

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: Is that a reply to something Guillaume said, or to my message?

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: yours

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: it is better than unicasting the 1628pb also.  but yeah, 80% seems like there's room for improvement but worthwhile imo.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: 80% offload is 80% fewer bytes. Maybe not optimal, but that's pretty darn good IMO

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: Needs moar optimization

chat.author: Max Franke
chat.text: He mentioned it is from "one of their customers", so I wonder if thats their best case or an average case

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: where in the network is this measured? If the mcast bits where uni'd instead how much traffic would that be?

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: I assume this is describing the difference between what's sent from cdn and what's received by set top boxes

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: So it's showing usage pattern - Everyone Love Mcast! - and not anything about BW?

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: Not sure I understand you

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: It is comparing the actual bytes transmitted (339 PB) to what would have to have been transmitted if it weren't leveraging multicast (1628 PB)

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: There! That's what I thought he was trying to say. But the numbers were given as-is and not as-if

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: Yes, I heard that as reported by set top box as received. That might differ from as-if, but should be roughly similar probably under normal conditions

chat.author: Greg Shepherd
chat.text: Ok, great bit from the auto note-taker: (S, G) is not Eskimo Cheese

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: tho with abr it's possible it could differ very substantially in practice, but represents a legitimately higher qos achieved for that comparison, so an "as-if" interpretation is very handwavy wrt what the real world would do.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: Oh, yeah, good point. Bad QoE could have driven that 1628 far lower.

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: right.  in practice you can imagine the unicast cdn maybe could only do like 800 and thus people would get a half-bitrate feed or whatever, depending what their links and servers can do.  all very complicated, so they just report "as-is" on what was actually received and let you draw your own inferences, because it's kind of all you can do.  been there.

chat.author: Kyle Rose
chat.text: Seems like it's better to compare as-if rather than as-is, since the customers presumably want to pull at least as good video as they actually did in the multicast-enabled scenario

chat.text: for the record, 100gbps is way faster than i ever got my relay to run, this seems very probably the better amt approach.

chat.text: lenny, was there any bgp extension on dynamic tunnels?  The slides had something that sounded kinda like that (and vaguely like https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-jholland-idr-mcast-source-nexthop-over-amt/, tho I imagine there's some significant differences and that routing guys like yourselves would have taken the better approach comparing between the 2)

chat.text: Wasn't aware of that draft, will check it out, thx Jake.  Looks like it defined a new SAFI.  DIMT will use a new BGP attribute.

chat.author: Jake Holland
chat.text: Yes, I have no idea how practical the proposal was, I never took it to idr, just ran with dried instead after asking which one a network partner preferred
